target_customer: Lenders, banks and fintechs in Southeast Asia, later any document-heavy regulated business
problem: Lenders review bank statements and loan documents by hand, which is slow and lets fraud through. Fintelite extracts and checks the data automatically.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for document extraction and analysis, plus AI consulting

founders.name: Nadia Amalia
founders.background_notes: YC page bio; it describes her work at Sribuu.

founders.name: Nadia Fadhila
founders.background_notes: YC page: focuses on no-code OCR and rule-based automation and on marketing and sales; education and employers not listed.

investors: Angel investors including the Kopi Kenangan founder

technical_complexity.rationale: Template-free extraction from varied bank statement formats with OCR and rules was hard for a small team in 2021 before LLMs, though the underlying tools existed.

defensibility.rationale: Lender integrations create some lock-in, but OCR and later LLM extraction became widely available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced evidence of incumbents copying or acquiring it. Later local entrants such as Sxored (founded 2024) appeared.

market_need_then: Southeast Asian digital lenders were scaling loan approvals and fraud checks on bank statements; Fintelite's site cites customers such as KoinWorks speeding loan processing about 10x.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical AI for your documents; tagline Documents. Knowledge. Progress.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand; the name is easy to confuse with Fintel and similar fintech names, and the product is positioned as AI consulting beyond lending.

pivots.from: Lending-specific bank statement analysis and fraud detection
pivots.to: General AI document processing (AnyCheck), knowledge base and consulting
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred only from the current site versus the YC description, so treat as a positioning change.

outcome_analysis: Fintelite is active with about 20 staff and a customer list of regional banks and fintechs, but no priced round after a 2021 pre-seed of the sibling Sribuu was found. Public funding data is thin and aggregator figures conflict, so its trajectory is unclear. It appears to be a bootstrapped or lightly funded B2B tool that has broadened from lending to general document AI.
notes: The relationship to Sribuu is ambiguous: one summary calls Sribuu the earlier name while another says Sribuu continues as the consumer product and Fintelite is the B2B arm. The September 2021 pre-seed (BEENEXT, amount undisclosed) was reported for Sribuu. Aggregators give $500K and $815K totals and $4.2M 2024 revenue; these are unverified and not recorded. The DailySocial Fintelite OCR article returned 503. No competitor sources dated near the batch were found; the vendor search returned nothing dated 2021 or 2022. The pivot entry is an inference and flagged as such.
